fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,

paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

“We wanted to make the timetable easier to use without taking away the sessions that regular swimmers rely on,” said centre manager Priya Shah. “The comments we received helped us see where a small shift could make a real difference.” The centre tested a draft schedule with its swimming instructors and the Alderwick Swim Club before confirming the final times. The club asked that its Tuesday training slot remain unchanged, and that request has been accommodated.

1. Weekday sessions

The pool opens at 6:30 a.m. from Monday to Friday. Lane swimming runs from 6:30 to 8:30 a.m., with four lanes available throughout and a fifth lane reserved for lessons on Wednesday mornings. The former lunchtime lane session has moved from 12:00 noon to 12:30 p.m. and now ends at 2:00 p.m. This gives the morning school group time to leave the changing area before public swimming begins. Public swimming continues from 2:00 to 3:30 p.m. on weekdays, except on Thursday, when a beginner lesson uses the shallow end until 2:30 p.m.

After-school lessons take place from 3:45 to 5:45 p.m. on Monday, Wednesday and Friday. The main pool is divided between classes and public lane swimming during those hours, so visitors should expect fewer open lanes than in the morning. Tuesday’s club training remains at 6:00 p.m., while the Wednesday adult lesson has moved to 6:15 p.m. Evening public swimming is available from 7:00 to 8:30 p.m. on Monday and Thursday. On Friday, the pool closes to the public at 7:30 p.m. for staff training and maintenance.

2. Weekend and family swimming

Saturday’s first family session begins at 9:00 a.m., half an hour earlier than before. A second family session runs from 1:00 to 3:00 p.m., and the shallow end is available throughout both periods. The centre has kept the Saturday 10:00 a.m. lane-swimming session, but it now finishes at 11:30 a.m. rather than noon. This leaves staff time to reset the pool before the family session begins.

On Sunday, family swimming is scheduled from 10:00 a.m. to noon, followed by public swimming from noon to 2:00 p.m. Lane swimming is available from 2:00 to 4:00 p.m. The pool’s inflatable equipment will be used during the last 30 minutes of the Sunday family session, subject to staff availability. Visitors who need a quieter environment can ask reception about the sensory-friendly hour, which takes place on the first Sunday of each month from 9:00 to 10:00 a.m. The centre limits numbers for that session and asks participants to book in advance.

The timetable also includes two weekly sessions for older adults. These run on Tuesday and Thursday from 10:30 to 11:30 a.m., with a section of the pool set aside for gentle exercise and supported entry. The sessions are open to swimmers with different levels of experience; instructors can offer basic guidance, but they do not provide individual therapy. A carer may accompany a participant in the water when needed, provided both people meet the centre’s usual admission and safety requirements.

3. Lessons, access and booking

Children’s lessons continue in six-week blocks, and current pupils keep their existing places unless their families request a change. New lesson enquiries can be made at reception or through the council’s leisure portal. The centre expects the next block to begin in June, although places depend on instructor availability and each child’s assessed level. Families should not attend a lesson before receiving a confirmed day and time.

The accessible changing room remains open during all public sessions. A pool hoist is available, and visitors who need it are encouraged to call ahead so staff can check that the equipment is ready and arrange assistance with entry. The centre has not changed its admission prices. Adult and child tickets can still be bought at reception, while members may scan their cards at the entrance. Booking is not required for ordinary public swimming, but advance booking is recommended for lessons and the sensory-friendly hour.

Printed copies of the timetable are available at Alderwick Baths and the library on Market Street. The online version includes a calendar view that can be filtered by lane swimming, family sessions or lessons; staff update it if a one-off closure is necessary.
